MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Hospital

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Age at Testing: 1 day
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Suspected Down syndrome in newborn

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Rapid aneuploidy screening for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21

SPECIMEN
Type: Whole blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

RESULT: ABNORMAL

Trisomy 21 detected

DETAILED FINDINGS

Chromosome 21: TRISOMY DETECTED
Five informative markers demonstrated three alleles or diallelic ratios consistent with trisomy:
• D21S11 (21q21.1): Triallelic pattern
• D21S1409 (21q21.2): Diallelic ratio 2:1
• D21S1435 (21q21.3): Triallelic pattern
• D21S1442 (21q21.3): Diallelic ratio 2:1
• D21S1411 (21q22.3): Triallelic pattern

Chromosome 13: Normal complement (two copies)
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns

Chromosome 18: Normal complement (two copies)
All markers showed normal biallelic patterns

MOLECULAR KARYOTYPE
rsa(13,18)x2,(21)x3

INTERPRETATION
This QF-PCR analysis demonstrates trisomy for chromosome 21, which is diagnostic of Down syndrome. The finding of five informative markers with consistent trisomic patterns provides robust confirmation of the diagnosis. The normal complement for chromosomes 13 and 18 excludes trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome) and trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome).

The molecular findings are consistent with the clinical suspicion of Down syndrome in this newborn patient.

LIMITATIONS
• This test detects whole chromosome aneuploidies only
• Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
• Segmental imbalances, translocations, and other structural rearrangements are not detected by this method
• This test does not exclude other chromosomal or genetic abnormalities

RECOMMENDATIONS
• Follow-up testing at a regional genetics laboratory is recommended for comprehensive genetic evaluation
• Genetic counseling is advised to discuss implications for the family
• Clinical correlation with phenotypic features is recommended

Authorized by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
